messages:
Maria: Heads-up: a live deploy yesterday tried to hot-swap in-place quantized overlays and we served a mixed shard for ~30s before the rollout killed it. Root cause looked like a partial overlay write + loader rebind race. Need a robust "shadow-swap" protocol for patching shards without risking partial views.
Arjun: Oof. Can you summarize the sequence that led to the mixed view?
Maria: Publisher uploaded overlay -> CDN warmed -> orchestrator kicked reload -> loader attempted atomic mmap remap while overlay still being copied to object store (the copy completed after the name change). Result: some readers used old map, others raced to new, and eviction + remap timing made it worse.
Devin: We should require a two-phase publish: stage -> verify -> promote. Promotion must be a single atomic manifest edit referencing a content-addressed token. Loaders only switch on seeing the token referenced in the manifest. No blind filename swaps.
Sparrow: Add to that: a small immutable "promotion token" object that contains checksums and a CAS id. Manifest update references token_id. Loaders fetch token metadata and validate before switching. That avoids relying on filesystem rename semantics across CDN/origin layers.
Chao: Implementation constraints: we must support streaming loaders that do range reads. Promotion should include a list of per-shard chunk checksums or a chunked-merkle root so in-flight range readers can validate on the fly.
Arjun: For memory-efficient quant overlays, we prefer an indirection table: overlay has a compact diff + remap map. We must ensure the remap application is idempotent and observable atomically by the loader. How do we make the remap atomic without copying the whole shard?
Devin: Approach: loader maintains a remap pointer table in memory that is swapped atomically (pointer swap) once the new overlay passes verification. The on-disk overlay is persisted as immutable shards; loader keeps a small in-memory overlay descriptor that maps logical chunk -> physical location. When promote happens, publish the new overlay descriptor via the promotion token.
Sparrow: So steps: 1) publisher uploads immutable overlay shards + token containing descriptor & checksums; 2) token verified by control plane; 3) manifest updated to reference token_id; 4) loader sees manifest change, fetches token, validates shards, then atomically swap in-memory descriptor; 5) old descriptor retained until refcount hits 0 and then garbage-collected.
Maria: That solves the mixed view problem through atomic descriptor swap. Need to make sure descriptor fetch/verify is cheap: include small header with uncompressed_size_hint and shard chunk_count so loader can pre-allocate.
Chao: Eviction interplay: if overlay application requires additional pages, we should have a graceful fallback: attempt descriptor swap only if sufficient resident set available; otherwise demote to background staging and apply lazily per-chunk on access. Mark descriptor as "lazy_applied" so readers know they'll get on-demand materialization.
Arjun: UX for publishers: we should provide a client-side tool that produces promotion token with chunked hashes and signs it. Support both full-apply (eager) and lazy-apply modes. Manifest should carry a field like "overlay_mode": "eager|lazy" per token reference.
Sparrow: Also expose "gc_grace_seconds" on token so loaders don't reclaim old descriptors too soon; gives in-flight queries time to drain. Default maybe 300s.
Maria: Proposal manifest snippet (for discussion):
```json
{
  "model": "mpt-30b",
  "shards": [
    {"path":"m.safetensors.000","token_id":"tok:sha256:abc123","overlay_mode":"eager","gc_grace_seconds":300}
  ]
}
```
Devin: Loader behavior: on manifest change, fetch token metadata (not the full shard) to validate checksums and sizes. If token references lazy mode, keep serving old descriptor until chunks are fetched and remapped on-demand. If eager, try to apply but fall back to lazy if eviction blocks progress. Emit metric shard.overlay.apply_mode = {eager_success,eager_fallback,lazy}.
Chao: For in-place remap path that avoids full rehydration, make sure remap table format is compact and has a version field. Loaders must ignore unknown versions and refuse to apply a remap they don't understand. That lets us evolve remap encoding.
Arjun: How do we protect against a publisher reusing token_id accidentally after key rotation or redeploy? Token IDs should be content-addressed (hash of descriptor+signing key id) and manifest includes manifest_pubkey_id. Loader verifies signature, then validates token content hash matches token_id.
Sparrow: Ops/telemetry: track overlay.apply_attempts, overlay.apply_mode, overlay.gc_trash_size, overlay.verify_failures. ops-bot can create the dashboard ticket.
ops-bot: Created INF-4011: "Overlay promotion tokens and loader metrics". Will emit metrics: overlay.apply.attempts, overlay.apply.mode, overlay.verify.failures, overlay.gc.reclaimed_bytes.
Maria: Back-compat: if manifest references no token, loader assumes single-stage legacy behavior. We add token_id as optional. Loader must tolerate both.
Devin: Security note: require manifest signature for any token-based promotion. For hosted we can enforce mandatory signing; for dedicated, make it opt-in.
Chao: Testing: simulate partial token publish (token visible but shards incomplete), publisher mis-signing, and fast GC reclaim. Also validate lazy apply correctness under heavy eviction.
Maria: Action items: Arjun to draft spec for promotion token + descriptor format; Devin to sketch loader descriptor-swap implementation; Sparrow + Chao to add sim and telemetry stubs; ops-bot tracking INF-4011; I'll run a small canary once prototype is ready.
Arjun: I'll push a spec PR with examples for remap table layout and token signature format.
Sparrow: I'll prototype the atomic pointer swap and the lazy_apply path in the loader shim.
Maria: Thanks everyone. This should make hotpatches safe and predictable. :thumbsup:
